text:
Artificial intelligence has the potential to expand educational access across national and linguistic boundaries. Translation tools, online tutoring systems, and digital learning platforms can make knowledge available to students regardless of location. However, global access does not guarantee equal quality or cultural relevance.

One major benefit of AI is language support. Automated translation and speech tools can help students access materials that were previously available only in widely spoken languages. Learners may also receive explanations in their preferred language, improving understanding and participation.

AI-powered platforms can support students in regions where qualified teachers or specialist subjects are limited. A learner in a remote community may access lessons in mathematics, science, or coding that are unavailable locally. Such systems may reduce geographical barriers and extend educational opportunity.

However, AI-generated materials often reflect the cultures and assumptions represented in their training data. Examples, historical perspectives, and social values may be drawn mainly from dominant countries. As a result, students may receive content that ignores local knowledge or presents one cultural viewpoint as universal.

Infrastructure also remains a major challenge. Reliable electricity, internet access, devices, and technical support are unevenly distributed. Global education initiatives that depend heavily on AI may exclude communities without these resources.

Local educators should therefore be involved in adapting AI-supported materials. Content must be checked for accuracy, language quality, cultural relevance, and alignment with local curricula.

AI can support global education by reducing barriers of language and distance. Nevertheless, access must be accompanied by infrastructure, local participation, and cultural sensitivity. Global education should not simply distribute standardised AI content but should combine international knowledge with local needs and perspectives.
